scope: 0x66EC30 is a standard LSB-first bit reader, so id 4048 cannot come from bits 1309..1320 - which means the probe's stream pointer is not the one used for the id read

the_reader_assembly.0x66EC8D: cmp ecx,[esi+0x10] ; jge -> zero if the byte index is past the bound
the_reader_assembly.0x66EC96: eax = [esi+8] ; eax = byte [eax+ecx]  - the buffer is [esi+8] and the index is [+0x20] >> 3
the_reader_assembly.0x66ECA3: shr eax, cl  with cl = [+0x20] & 7       - align the byte so the requested bit becomes bit 0
the_reader_assembly.0x66ECA5: ecx = 8 - offset                            - bits available in this byte
the_reader_assembly.0x66ECB1: if N <= available: [+0x20] += N and return (byte & mask)
the_reader_assembly.0x66ECCB: else: consume the available bits, [+0x20] = (N_remaining + byte_cursor*8), and continue

conclusion_about_the_encoding: the reader is a plain LSB-first bit reader over the byte buffer at [esi+8]
so a 12-bit read starting at bit 1309 returns exactly the 12 bits at 1309..1320
what_that_leaves: the read that produced 4048 did not start at bit 1309 of the same stream

the most likely reason is that the probe's `esi` at 0x6716C3 is not the stream used by 0x671650 for the id read - the probe samples whatever esi holds at the loop-exit instruction, which may already be a different register role
so the earlier '20 bits for a 12-bit read' measurement is suspect for the same reason: the two samples may come from different stream objects
the_clean_way_to_settle_the_id_question: probe inside 0x671650 itself (for example at 0x66ECA1, right after the byte fetch) and log [esi+8], [+0x20] and the returned value
that ties the value to the exact position and buffer, with the same esi the decoder uses
